To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of a database management system or database machine can be evaluated in a multiuser system by using a workload model that includes a transaction mix, a multiprogramming level and a degree of data sharing; and that the performance of such systems can be evaluated using a small number of basic query types.

(1) the performance of a database system is a function of the multiprogramming level and the amount and nature of the data sharing among simultaneously executed transactions; (2) the performance of the Britton-Lue IDM 500 database computer is comparable to that of a conventional database system; and (3) a database benchmark should include only four basic types of queries.

the performance of database systems and database machines under a wide variety Of workloads, and the methodology that we have developed is applicable to any database management system.
